claims.claim_vi: A quadtree partitions 2D space by recursively subdividing it into four quadrants until a criterion is met; it is an in-memory structure built at LBS server start-up, not a database.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source splits until no node has more than 100 businesses; a search descends to the leaf containing the origin and adds neighbours' businesses if the leaf has fewer than 100.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source says building the tree for 200 million businesses may take a few minutes, during which the server cannot serve traffic, hence incremental rollout.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit; the figure was not reproduced by the lesson.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19: Python 3, bucket capacity 100, seed 7; uniform points: 100k -> 2,221 leaves, depth 6, mean 45.0 points per leaf; 1M -> 16,384 leaves, depth 7, mean 61.0. Clustered (20 Gaussian clusters): 100k -> 2,668 leaves, depth 11, mean 37.5; 1M -> 21,583 leaves, depth 13, mean 46.3. Share of 2,000 queries (at data points) landing in a leaf with fewer than 100 points: 95.8%, 100%, 99.2%, 99.3%. Build time for 1M points 3.5 s (uniform) and 4.8 s (clustered).
claims.verified_by: Script embedded verbatim in the lesson (details block); run in the session and results copied from its output.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung đều là các bước đánh số: xây cây và tìm quán. Kết quả thử nghiệm nằm trong bảng của bài, không vẽ.
source_deviations: The source's two figures are not reproduced; the lesson draws its own steps.
The lesson adds an experiment on leaf occupancy and depth, and a question about whether neighbour leaves guarantee the nearest 100 (author's reasoning).
The source's 'few minutes for 200M businesses' is reported but not verified.
